Conductor UI review: examples

2026-11-04 · full findings in README.md (UXR-22..89) · PR #150

The board is the product and it reads well; what holds the UI back is raw engine ids on every screen, every request styled as an alarm, a cramped desktop detail panel, and no shared pattern for overlays and editors. Each example below puts a crop of today’s screen next to an HTML mock-up of the proposed fix.

Board and ticket

Cards speak in titles, not engine ids

S2 MUXR-30 · UXR-31 · UXR-33

Cards repeat the column in raw state ids (implement, build, await_approval) and badges wrap into two-line blobs. Show a state title only when it differs from the column, keep badges on one line, and give each card at most one action.

Requests styled by kind; only failures are red

S2 MUXR-35 · UXR-36 · UXR-39 · UXR-32

A question, a finished agent asking for review, a permission prompt and a real failure all share one pink “ACTION NEEDED” block. When everything is red, nothing is. Give each kind its colour, verb and buttons; the composer knows what it is answering.

The rules builder opens on a summary, in sections

S1 MUXR-60 · UXR-61 · UXR-62 · UXR-63

A transition with rules is one ~2,000 px column in a 380 px panel: unlabelled check rows (“10m”), unlabelled condition parameters (“5m”, “1”, “resolution”, “ci”), unavailable options, raw action ids, and “When not met” last. Start with a sentence that says what the transition does; put each part in a section with a count; label every field.

Implementing › Ready for testing

Implementing → Waiting external

When the agent says Ready for testing (work tickets): set up with auto-detect, run Build passes and Tests pass, have a reviewer check 1 item, open a PR, then wait up to 3 days for PR checks and 1 approval → Waiting external. If not met: back to Implementing with your instruction, up to 3 times, then Needs input.

Mock-ups use the app’s light-theme tokens (packages/web/src/styles.css); their names and numbers are illustrative, and they are proposals for Ben’s review, not built UI. Severity: S1 blocks the job or looks broken, S2 slows it or confuses, S3 polish. Size: S small change, M a ticket, L a project.
